video_title: HUGE Growth In Australian Basketball: Breaking Down The Hoops Scene in Melbourne

quotes.speaker: Derek Rucker
quotes.summary_phrase: Derek Rucker on the stigma of shooting three-pointers in the 80s
quotes.excerpt: Every time I shot a three it was frowned upon, irrespective of the result.
quotes.quote: In an era whereby every time I took a three-point shot because it wasn't an acceptable part of the game yet, every time I shot a three it was frowned upon, irrespective of the result. So we shot it under a lot of duress from your coach. My coach was never happy when I made a three.

quotes.speaker: Cole Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Cole Anthony on the NBL atmosphere feeling like a college game
quotes.excerpt: It honestly reminded me of playing back like I was in college again.
quotes.quote: It honestly reminded me of playing back like I was in college again, like a nice college game, like against Duke. So I got a lot of respect, and they outplayed us yesterday and they got a go, though.

quotes.speaker: Cole Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Cole Anthony on the intensity of NBL fans compared to NBA
quotes.excerpt: The fans here are just as loud, they care just as much about the game.
quotes.quote: Definitely in the NBA you're going to have some bigger arenas, but the fans here are just as loud, they care just as much about the game. And you know, it's really not that big a difference. At the end of the day when you step on that court, my focus is going to be on the court.

quotes.speaker: Cole Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Cole Anthony on the business reality of the NBA
quotes.excerpt: When you get to the NBA, you're confronted with the brutal reality that this is a business.
quotes.quote: When you get to the NBA, you're confronted with the brutal reality that this is a business first and foremost. And a lot of times business can just get in the way of your joy or the way you think about the game. For me, I know that's definitely something that's happened.

quotes.speaker: Cole Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Cole Anthony on why players might reject contract extensions
quotes.excerpt: I can understand why he didn't take that money at first.
quotes.quote: I can understand why he didn't take that money at first. I know he's looking at the other dudes in his draft class who got more money than him. Because that's the one thing, everybody in this joint is competitive. And it's not just about the on-the-court stuff, it's about the off-the-court stuff, it's about the money, it's about all that.

quotes.speaker: Cole Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Cole Anthony on the emotional weight of contract negotiations
quotes.excerpt: I was in there just going, I was in there hooping, but I was so pissed.
quotes.quote: We had a practice and I was in there just going, I was in there hooping, but I was so pissed. I almost started crying at practice. I was just so worked up, so emotional, so just in the practice. Now I was killing dudes in there, but it was just one of those things where I'm like, yo, am I really going to wait another year and sacrifice potentially making all this money?

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Olgun Uluc on the high-level talent in the NBL
quotes.excerpt: We may be in the golden era of point guards.
quotes.quote: Coming to play in this league right now where we may be in the golden era of point guards and the guys that he is going to have to face: Bryce Cotton, Kendrick Davis, Cole Anthony, Taran Armstrong, Arnald Velicka up in Brisbane, who was the Lithuanian League MVP last year, he's leading the league in assists. Then they got Brandon Knight coming in. It is such high-quality depth at the position.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Olgun Uluc on the NBL's growing international reputation
quotes.excerpt: The respect level of it that it has internationally has grown.
quotes.quote: The NBL I feel like is in a really good place right now. The respect level of it that it has internationally has grown and the NBA is looking to the NBL for more than just players.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Olgun Uluc on NBA teams hiring NBL coaches
quotes.excerpt: We have a coach in the NBL, his name is Josh King.
quotes.quote: We have a coach in the NBL, his name is Josh King. He's head coach of the Southeast Melbourne Phoenix. He has this demeanor on the court where he plays, his demeanor is like how he coaches, right? He's got high energy, he's animated. Someone dives on the floor next to him, he's almost diving on the floor with them to pick them up. I was told that over the off-season, when the Portland Trail Blazers had a vacant head coach position, they interviewed Josh King. Josh King had a 90-minute Zoom interview with Tom Dunton, the new owner of the Portland Trail Blazers.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Proctor's growing role and impact on the Boomers roster
quotes.excerpt: They've cleared some of their roster out to give Tyrese Proctor more of a runway.
quotes.quote: I think Tyrese Proctor will make the team. They love Tyrese Proctor in Cleveland. I can tell you they are already making a big impact. They've cleared some of their roster out to give Tyrese Proctor more of a runway.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: The Boomers face uncertainty regarding Patty Mills' international future
quotes.excerpt: For the Boomers, again, there's the Patty Mills void that will need to be filled.
quotes.quote: For the Boomers, again, there's the Patty Mills void that will need to be filled. That's also a question that needs to be answered, whether Patty Mills is part of the World Cup team and ultimately him going to a sixth Olympics. That is a question that's yet to be answered. But Tyrese Proctor theoretically fills that.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the imperfect options for the Boomers' four spot
quotes.excerpt: The most interesting question with the Boomers is the four spot, because all of them are imperfect.
quotes.quote: The most interesting question with the Boomers is the four spot, because there are so many options that it could be, but all of them are imperfect. So you have Jack McVeigh started at the four spot in the last major tournament. He is a lights-out shooter, he is a no-leave shooter. But defensively he's not as good as someone like Matisse Thybulle, who is a high-level defender, but he's not particularly a shooter, especially at the FIBA level. And then you have someone like Johnny Furphy, who's coming off an injury. He's like a legit 6'9". I've stood next to him, he's huge. But is he at the level? Is Alex Toohey the guy? Is he, he can do all those things, he can shoot, he can guard multiple positions, he's big, but is he high-level enough to play for the Boomers?

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Simmons' fit on the Australian World Cup team
quotes.excerpt: Ben Simmons has to play basketball first. There are other guys who have played way more basketball.
quotes.quote: Ben Simmons fits in that four spot, who again is imperfect because you have Ben Simmons, who is a non-shooter. He is big and can presumably still guard and he is athletic. I saw him when he came through here for the Boomers camp. He is huge. He is still athletic, but he is a non-shooter. Can you have a non-shooter on the floor when you have Josh Giddey, Dyson Daniels, Jock Landale? Jock Landale can shoot, but it feels like you do need some shooting firepower. Ben Simmons has to play basketball first. There are other guys who have played way more basketball in the last two, three, four years that you have to put more consideration into. If he plays basketball and he shows he is at the level and he wants to play for the Boomers, come on in. But until he plays meaningful basketball, you cannot make a serious case for him being on the team.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Team USA's World Cup qualification and roster challenges
quotes.excerpt: The most important thing to do with the World Cup, other than win it, is to qualify.
quotes.quote: The World Cup next year could be wide open. The Americans have not played well in the World Cup since the World Cup switched. The most important thing to do with the World Cup, other than win it, is to qualify for the Olympics. It is hard to qualify for the Olympics. Only 12 teams qualify for the Olympics, and the Americans have qualified for the last two Olympics by the skin of their teeth. That is a selling point that you tell your players: you want to be on the senior team, come to the World Cup because we need to qualify for the Olympics.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: France's automatic qualification for the 2024 Olympics
quotes.excerpt: France played poorly at the 2023 World Cup and would not have qualified for the Olympics.
quotes.quote: France played poorly at the 2023 World Cup and would not have qualified for the Olympics, but they were hosting so they were in. The Americans do not have the draw of saying 'come qualify for the Olympics,' and it is scheduled to be played in Qatar in August and September, where it is slightly warm. So the sales pitch to the Americans, I am not sure is going to be there. We will see.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Team USA's roster expectations for the 2024 World Cup
quotes.excerpt: I think it is going to be a bunch of young players that are trying to prove themselves.
quotes.quote: Do you think Team USA is not going to send anyone notable to this World Cup because they do not have to qualify for the Olympics? I think it is going to be a bunch of young players that are trying to prove themselves, but I do not think there is going to be—and we will see—I do not even know how many of the old guard are going to be in the.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Veterans on the previous Team USA World Cup roster
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson was on that team. Anthony Edwards was on that team. Tyrese Haliburton was on that team.
quotes.quote: Just like the last World Cup, Jalen Brunson was on that team. He did not play well, but Jalen Brunson was on that team. Anthony Edwards was on that team. Tyrese Haliburton was on that team. It was a step forward for a lot of those guys.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential young players for the next Team USA cycle
quotes.excerpt: I think maybe guys like Cooper Flagg, for example, guys who you anticipate being the next wave.
quotes.quote: I think maybe guys like Cooper Flagg, for example, guys who you anticipate being the next wave, but I do not know how many guys who have played in previous Olympics.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: The 2019 Team USA roster development
quotes.excerpt: There were a lot of real guys on that team, but they were not stars yet.
quotes.quote: I remember the 2019 team. It was guys like Kemba Walker was on the team, but Jaylen Brown was on that team, Jason Tatum, Donovan Mitchell. There were a lot of real guys on that team, but they were not stars yet. They had not fully developed into what they are now. So that is curious. For the Boomers, Australia sort of just gets to sit back because the top Oceania team from the World Cup gets through, and generally Australia does finish higher than New Zealand.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Gordie Herbert's roster rules for the Canadian team
quotes.excerpt: He can afford to not let Jamal Murray play because he is not committing to the entire cycle.
quotes.quote: We have spoken about this, Brian, about Gordie Herbert and his rule for his Canadian team going into this cycle. He has the—he can afford to not let Jamal Murray play because he is not committing to the entire cycle. I do not know if Adam Caporn, the new Boomers head coach, is able to say to any of the Australian guys, like, 'Hey, Josh Giddey, if you do not play in all of these things, including the qualifying games, then you cannot play.' Australia will take what it can get.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Gordie Herbert's roster requirements for Germany and Canada
quotes.excerpt: He told NBA players, multiple NBA players who did not show up, 'Sorry, we don't need you.'
quotes.quote: Gordie Herbert, who is the coach of the new coach of Canada, he has been the coach of Germany, and Germany, he put down a rule that said if you want to play in Paris in 24, you got to play in the Euro Championships and you got to play in the World Cup. And that progression led Germany to win the Euro Championships and the World Cup, but he told NBA players, multiple NBA players who did not show up, 'Sorry, we don't need you in the Olympics.' And he took over the Canadian team, he is Canadian, and he told the same rule, 'I want to see you in 26. If you want to show your face in Los Angeles in 28, I want to see you in 26 and I want to see you in 27.' And Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was out there this year playing for that. Two-time defending MVP went and played in World Cup qualification games because he wanted to qualify for 28, and some Canadians, including Jamal Murray, an All-Star, NBA champion, max NBA player, has been scratched from the list.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: The final roster spot for the Australian team
quotes.excerpt: You have two options. You can take Luke Paul, the up and coming star of Australian basketball.
quotes.quote: Let's say a team gets selected, there is 11 guys, you have a 12th spot, and it is basically a free spot. This guy probably is not going to play. You have two options. You can take Luke Paul, the up and coming star of Australian basketball, or you can take Matthew Dellavedova, the soon to be 35-year-old.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Dellavedova's role on the Australian team
quotes.excerpt: My prediction is that Matthew Dellavedova will be part of this World Cup team.
quotes.quote: My prediction is that Matthew Dellavedova will be part of this World Cup team, and he will scheme his way onto the Olympic team. And I say scheme in the kindest way, because as the 12th man, if you had to put Dellavedova on the floor, he will go and smother the best perimeter player and the best post player on the other team. If you saw him guard Jack McVeigh here in the NBL, he absolutely neutralized him. So he will go and do that for two minutes if he has to. You can trust him to bring the ball over the floor, and if he does not play a minute, he will wave a towel better than anyone has ever waved a towel in their life.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Anticipating Matthew Dellavedova defending Luke Paul
quotes.excerpt: I am looking forward to the first time Dellavedova defends Luke.
quotes.quote: I am looking forward to the first time Dellavedova defends Luke. I want to see how that experience goes.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Dellavedova's reputation as the 'Steph Stopper'
quotes.excerpt: I learned when I came to Australia that he is known as the Steph Stopper.
quotes.quote: I learned when I came to Australia that he is known as the Steph Stopper. I did not know that, but now that is what he has been bestowed in Australia as the Steph Stopper.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Dellavedova's defensive impact on Bryce Cotton
quotes.excerpt: There are some guys in the NBL who are long athletic wings. They are not close to what Dellavedova does.
quotes.quote: There are some guys in the NBL who are long athletic wings. They are not close to what Dellavedova does to Bryce Cotton as far as making his life a nightmare. A five-game series, Bryce Cotton just had to work so, so hard for every single shot.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Dellavedova's toughness and coffee habits
quotes.excerpt: He never ever complains about getting hurt. You kick him in the groin, elbow him in the head.
quotes.quote: Dellavedova, he brings his Australianness to the NBA in many ways. One, he never ever complains about getting hurt. You kick him in the groin, elbow him in the head, he never, he never looks phased at all because, you know, if you are Australian, you do not show like you are hurt, right? That is not the rugby way, you do not show injury. Secondly, the man guzzles coffee. My God, does Matthew Dellavedova love coffee. He is like one of the elite coffee drinkers, well he is not in the NBA now, but he was one of the elite coffee drinkers in the NBA, and I feel like that was, you know, bringing and, you know, sending the message, I can do this as an Australian.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Dellavedova's unique habits and 'grounding'
quotes.excerpt: He has gone through the grounding phase where he doesn't wear shoes.
quotes.quote: It feels like every year Dellavedova has like a new tonic that is the thing that helps him. Over the past couple years in the NBL, he has gone through the grounding phase where he does not wear shoes. He has gone through an oysters phase where he eats lots of oysters. I remember I spoke to Kendrick Davis, his superstar teammate. They hung out together in LA last off-season and Kendrick told me, 'Man, Dellavedova's kids just eat steaks all the time. Like my kids are eating like chocolates and candy. I look over at Dellavedova's kid, he has just got like a whole, a whole steak just like gnawing into it.'

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Steven Adams' unique eating habits
quotes.excerpt: Steven Adams' thing is he eats huge steaks with no utensils.
quotes.quote: This is Australia, not New Zealand, but you know, Steven Adams' thing is he eats huge steaks with no utensils, just with his, with his hands.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Steven Adams' birthplace and nationality
quotes.excerpt: Steven Adams was born in Australia but he was lost to the Kiwis.
quotes.quote: Steven Adams was born in Australia but he was lost to the Kiwis. He was lost.
